questions.solution: $\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1$ for all $\theta$.

questions.solution: $\cos^2 \theta = 1 - \tfrac{9}{25} = \tfrac{16}{25}$, so $\cos \theta = \tfrac{4}{5}$ (positive since $\theta$ is acute).

hints: Power rule for integration: $\int x^n \, dx = \tfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$.
questions.solution: $\int x^3 \, dx = \tfrac{x^4}{4} + C$. Always include $+C$ for indefinite integrals.

hints: Integrate term by term.
questions.solution: $\int 2x \, dx = x^2$, $\int 3 \, dx = 3x$. Sum: $x^2 + 3x + C$.

Evaluate at upper minus at lower.
FTC Part 1: $\tfrac{d}{dx}\int_0^x f(t) \, dt = f(x)$.
questions.solution: By the FTC, $F'(x)$ is the integrand evaluated at the upper limit: $F'(x) = x^2$.

questions.prompt: In a standard normal distribution, what % of data is within 1 standard deviation of the mean?
hints: Empirical (68-95-99.7) rule.
questions.solution: About 68% of data falls within $\pm 1\sigma$, 95% within $\pm 2\sigma$, 99.7% within $\pm 3\sigma$.

questions.prompt: A normal distribution has $\mu = 100$, $\sigma = 15$. What percent is below 115?
hints: 115 is one $\sigma$ above mean.
50% below mean, plus half of the 68% within $\pm 1\sigma$.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg ball moves at 3 m/s. Kinetic energy?
hints: $KE = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2$.

questions.prompt: A 5 kg object is 10 m above ground. PE? ($g \approx 10$ m/s²)
hints: $PE = mgh$.
questions.solution: $PE = 5 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 = 500$ J.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 6 m. Speed?
hints: $v = f \lambda$.

questions.prompt: Period of a wave with frequency 4 Hz?
$PV = nRT$. If P doubles at constant V and T, what happens to n?
hints: Solve $PV = nRT$ for $n$.
$n = PV/(RT)$.
questions.solution: At constant V, T: $n \propto P$. Doubling P doubles n.

questions.prompt: STP volume of 1 mole of ideal gas?
hints: Molar volume at STP.
questions.solution: 1 mole of any ideal gas at STP (0°C, 1 atm) occupies 22.4 L.

questions.prompt: Net ATP from one glucose via aerobic respiration (approx)?
hints: Total includes glycolysis + Krebs + ETC.
questions.solution: Roughly 30-32 ATP per glucose total (glycolysis 2, Krebs 2, ETC ~26-28).

questions.prompt: Where does the Krebs cycle occur?
hints: Krebs is the second stage of aerobic respiration.
questions.solution: The Krebs (citric acid) cycle takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.

questions.prompt: Max nodes in a binary tree of height $h$?
hints: Each level $i$ has at most $2^i$ nodes.
Sum from $i=0$ to $h$.

questions.prompt: Inorder traversal of BST visits nodes in what order?
hints: Inorder = left, root, right.
questions.solution: For a binary search tree, inorder traversal yields nodes in ascending sorted order — that's a key BST property.

hints: Divide-and-conquer: log n levels, n work per level.
questions.solution: Merge sort divides into halves ($\log n$ levels) and merges in $O(n)$ per level: total $O(n \log n)$.

hints: Worst case: bad pivot every time.
questions.solution: Quicksort's worst case is $O(n^2)$ when the pivot is consistently the smallest or largest element. Average is $O(n \log n)$.

hints: $\land$ is logical AND.
questions.solution: AND is true only when BOTH operands are true.

questions.prompt: Truth value of $\lnot(P \lor Q)$ when $P$ true, $Q$ false?
hints: Compute $P \lor Q$ first, then negate.
questions.solution: $P \lor Q = T \lor F = T$. Negate: $\lnot T = F$.

questions.prompt: How many ways to arrange 4 distinct books on a shelf?
hints: Permutation: $4!$.
questions.solution: $4! = 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 24$.

hints: $\binom{n}{k} = \tfrac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}$.

questions.prompt: For $AB$ to be defined, what must hold?
hints: Matrix multiplication requires inner dimensions to match.
questions.solution: If $A$ is $m \times n$ and $B$ is $p \times q$, then $AB$ is defined iff $n = p$ (cols of A = rows of B). Result is $m \times q$.

hints: Try a 2x2 example.
questions.solution: In general $AB \neq BA$. Even when both are defined and same size, they typically differ.

hints: Find largest int dividing both.
questions.solution: Divisors of 12: {1,2,3,4,6,12}. Divisors of 18: {1,2,3,6,9,18}. Largest common: 6.
